items.title: NEW — the `css { … }` block is UNUSABLE under the web prelude: its lowering seeds the chain with a bare `style` accessor (css.rs:93, `Node::Accessor("style")`), and `std::web` binds `style` to the ambient MODULE, so every block in a `prelude = "std::web"` package fails with "`style` is a module, not a value; qualify through it (`style::item`)" (kolt channel.vl:71); the element lowering's bare `view` survives only because the prelude's `view` is the function — both desugarings are scope-DEPENDENT where they should be hygienic
items.discussion: the owner's find (2026-09-07), reproduced in a scratch web-prelude package; kolt has zero css blocks for this reason
items.status: OPEN — the owner's find (2026-09-07); blocks the css-block push
items.body: Lower the seed (and the element form's `view`) to a scope-independent reference to the std item — the macro engine's hygienic std references are the precedent — so a block means `std::style::style()` whatever `style` names at the site, and `<div>` means `std::ui::view` whatever `view` names. Pins: a css block under `std::web` (the ambient module), under a local `let style = …`, under `import std::style::style as s` with no other `style` in scope, and with no prelude at all; the element form under a local `view` binding. Interim for kolt until it lands: a per-file `import std::style::{ Color, Length, style };` shadows the ambient module inside that file (probed), at the cost of writing `Length::rem` instead of `style::Length::rem` there — both spellings cannot coexist in one file.
